shared_text:
The flight. A regional jet on a passenger flight, landing in the evening after a visual approach. The aircraft was lighter because there were fewer passengers. The report does not give the weather.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying and the captain the pilot monitoring.

What happened. The approach was stable on the visual glide path to the runway. The first officer began the landing flare, and the aircraft floated further than the first officer expected. To correct this and land, the first officer held the pitch attitude or even lowered it. The main wheels touched down at or just beyond the last touchdown zone marking. The first officer began to pull the reverse thrust triggers and levers to deploy the thrust reversers. At that moment the captain called for a go-around. The first officer did not start the go-around at once, and looked to see whether the reversers had deployed. The captain then took control of the aircraft to complete the landing.
safe_outcome: The captain completed the landing, and the aircraft stopped on the runway without further incident. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: The aircraft could not be stopped on the remaining runway. It left the end of the runway at about 30 knots and came to rest on the grass. The passengers were evacuated, and two received minor injuries during the evacuation. The aircraft was slightly damaged.
notes: Rule 3 removed: "fixating on landing" (replaced by the observable actions: holding or lowering the pitch to correct the float and land), "I hesitated" (replaced by "did not start the go-around at once"), and the hedged cause "potentially me starting the rotation high". Kept from the cause sentence as a fact: the aircraft was lighter because there were fewer passengers. Judgement call: the touchdown at or just beyond the last touchdown-zone marking is kept in the shared text. Where they touched down is normally safe-ending material, but here the crew's later actions (selecting reverse, the captain's go-around call, the change of control) follow from it, and it does not contradict the bad ending. Safe ending: the report stops at the captain taking control "to complete the landing"; that the aircraft then stopped on the runway without further incident is inferred from the absence of any excursion or damage in the coded fields. No weather or light is coded; "in the evening" is from the 1801-2400 time block. The coded anomaly "loss of aircraft control" is not described in the narrative and was not added.
